Customer requires SOC 2 Type II evidence, interested in ISO 27001 roadmap, SSO with Okta (SAML 2.0), fine-grained RBAC, and immutable audit logs with 13+ months retention. transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-14
Start: 15:00 EST
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Redwood CSM), Mark Reynolds (Parkview CTO), Sara Gomez (Parkview CISO), David Lin (Parkview Director, Platform), Emily Park (VP Clinical Ops)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy): Discussed SOC 2 and ISO evidence, SAML/Okta setup, RBAC and audit logs, benchmark plan and success criteria for pilot. Next: Redwood to send security artifacts, run benchmarks, schedule follow-up.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll kick us off. um quick roll call, and then we want to confirm security bar and pilot success criteria for the POC.
[00:12] Mark: thanks Alex, Mark here, Sara's on from security. we're looking to validate you for a small pilot that will touch PHI-ish data, so security is obviously the gating factor.
[00:22] Sara: yeah hi, quick note, Parkview needs SOC 2 Type II evidence, and we'd like to understand your ISO posture as well. also SSO with Okta, SAML, RBAC, and detailed audit logs - that's a must.
[00:34] Alex: totally, that's helpful. we are SOC 2 Type II, we'll send the report and the SSP. on ISO 27001 we're in progress - roadmap in our security pack. we also offer both hosted API and Dedicated/Private options if you need data residency - we can run pilot in a VPC.
[00:48] Sara: can you confirm what data is retained in logs for hosted? we can't have PHI persisted without controls.
[00:55] Priya: short answer, by default we redact and we have options - for POC we can either enable redaction and short retention or spin up a Private instance where logs are customer-owned. sorry, there's a bit of a jumble - so, the hosted API by default retains minimal metadata for 30 days for debugging, but we have a no-retention option and dedicated plans where logs stay in your VPC.
[01:20] David: ok, goal is no PHI in Redwood logs for the pilot. we'll confirm exact fields but likely free-text clinical notes will be considered PHI.
[01:28] Liam: understood. for the pilot we recommend either: (a) hosted with redaction + signed DPA + no-retention config, or (b) Dedicated reserved capacity so traffic and logs are isolated, or (c) full Private on-prem - which is heavier.
[01:40] Emily: timeline - we want to start pilot in the next two weeks if security signs off.
[01:45] Alex: that's tight but doable. quick question on success criteria - what does Parkview need to see to consider this successful?
[01:52] Mark: three things: security pass (SOC2/SSO/RBAC/audit logs), performance - must handle our throughput with acceptable latency, and integration with our Okta SAML SSO.
[02:03] Sara: and a clearly documented data flow and attestation that no PHI is stored.
[02:08] Priya: for performance, can you share expected QPS and typical prompt sizes? that'll let us size the test and recommend model/quantization/profiles.
[02:17] David: typical traffic for the pilot - about 50 req/s peak, average token size per request ~600 tokens (prompt + completion), and 95th percentile latency target we'd like under 500ms but ideally sub-300ms.
[02:32] Priya: good, that's useful. rough ballpark: on our hosted fleet with a medium-sized open model and sane batching you'd see median latencies ~200-400ms depending on model and batch policy. Dedicated GPUs can drop tail latency and give more predictable throughput. we'll run benchmarks to confirm.
[02:47] Mark: can you quantify cost tradeoffs? if we need Dedicated for predictability what's the estimate?
[02:53] Alex: we'll follow up with formal pricing but expect Dedicated reserved capacity monthly commit - we'll send a sizing and cost spreadsheet after we run a benchmark using your sample workload.
[03:05] Sara: on SSO, we use Okta, SAML 2.0. we need IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows, SCIM for provisioning would be great for teams.
[03:16] Priya: we support SAML 2.0, SP/IdP flows, and SCIM for provisioning, and we can share our Okta integration guide. RBAC model supports roles at org/route/model level - can enforce least privilege.
[03:30] Sara: any MFA requirements for admin access?
[03:33] Maya: yes, we enforce SSO with enforced MFA for admin roles on enterprise accounts; we can enforce IP restrictions and device policies via Okta as well.
[03:42] David: audit logs - what fields and retention options exist? we need immutable logs with user, action, timestamp, request id, model version, and ideally a hash of content or indication if PHI was present. retention needs to be 13 months for us.
[03:55] Priya: our audit logs include actor, action, timestamp, request id, model id/version, and outcome. for hosted we can provide log export to your SIEM, we also have immutable append-only logs for Dedicated/Private. retention configurable; 13 months is standard enterprise option.
[04:12] Mark: perfect. what's the workflow for legal/compliance review? we'd need a DPA and subprocessor list.
[04:19] Alex: we'll send the DPA draft and subprocessor list along with SOC2 artifacts. legal can review and we'll triage any questions.
[04:26] Emily: benchmarks - what will you test?
[04:29] Liam: we'll run throughput/latency tests at 50 req/s with your token distribution (we'll request a small sample, sanitized). we'll test a few model sizes: 7B quantized, 13B quantized, and a performance-optimized variant; measure median, p50/p95, and cost per 1k tokens.
[04:46] Mark: do you support KV cache and prefix caching? we rely on session context caching for chat flows.
[04:52] Priya: yes we support KV cache and prefix/KV caching; note sometimes a transcribed doc calls it KV cash in the logs - ignore that, ha. caching helps reduce repeated compute; we'll include cache hit-rate in benchmark outputs.
[05:05] Sara: encryption at rest and in transit? KMS?
[05:07] Alex: yes TLS in transit, encryption at rest using customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private; hosted supports our KMS and we offer Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) options on enterprise plans.
[05:18] David: what about certifications - you said SOC 2 Type II; timeline for ISO 27001?
[05:23] Alex: SOC 2 Type II completed last quarter, report will be attached. ISO 27001 is in progress - we have a planned audit late Q2, but we'll include the roadmap.
[05:33] Sara: any prior healthcare customers references?
[05:35] Alex: yes, we can share redacted references and case studies - will do that in the follow-up packet.
[05:42] Priya: small note: for the pilot we often recommend a hybrid approach - run initial bench on hosted with redaction and no-retention then switch to Dedicated if tail-latency/cost require it.
[05:54] Mark: that sounds reasonable. if we can get security artifacts and a bench that proves sub-300ms median with 50 req/s we'll greenlight a two-week pilot.
[06:03] Emily: and we'll need a roll-off plan if things go sideways.
[06:06] Alex: yes we'll include rollback/fallback policies and a canary plan for the pilot.
[06:12] David: questions about data flow - can you provide a network diagram?
[06:15] Priya: absolutely - we'll include a network and data flow diagram showing options for routed traffic, VPC peering, and Private on-prem.
[06:24] Mark: ok let's recap next steps and owners.
[06:27] Alex: recap: Alex send SOC2 + SSP + DPA draft, Priya send SAML/Okta guide and RBAC examples, Liam provision test cluster and run benchmarks week of Feb 21, Parkview to send sample workload and confirm PHI fields, legal to review DPA. follow-up meeting scheduled after benchmarks.
[06:42] Sara: we'll also assign internal stakeholders to review the security docs - expect questions from our security operations team.
[06:49] Alex: great, thanks all. we'll aim to get artifacts out by Tuesday.
[06:53] (end)

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker labels generic, small mishears (KV cache -> KV cash), timestamps approximate.
